notes: Installed from canonical-strategy track. Strategies remain as authored; webapp does not synthesize them.

SPR_vs_SP_Sub_v2.start: Enemy Rogue, with enemy Priest Sap/control.
SPR_vs_SP_Sub_v2.objective: Threaten Rogue while drawing escapes that can also enable a controlled Priest attack.
SPR_vs_SP_Sub_v2.win: Rogue damage with Priest disrupted, or Priest damage with Rogue contained.
SPR_vs_SP_Sub_v2.create: Build Rogue pressure; after its escape, confirmed Blind → Priest attack → Sap is a recurring sequence.
SPR_vs_SP_Sub_v2.convert: That Priest line is a documented option; its priority over renewed Rogue damage is unknown.
SPR_vs_SP_Sub_v2.alternative: Stay Rogue through partial heals; renew Priest control or interrupt healing. Priest-first also occurs.
SPR_vs_SP_Sub_v2.failure: Friendly Priest death can end the team attempt before or after escape extraction.
SPR_vs_SP_Sub_v2.reset: Survive countercontrol, rebuild damage/control, and distinguish a trade or solo continuation from a two-player finish.

SPR_vs_Arms_HPal_v2.objective: Threaten a Warrior finish and draw escapes while building a later Paladin commitment.
SPR_vs_Arms_HPal_v2.win: Paladin stun/damage with Warrior contained; protection may require another attempt.
SPR_vs_Arms_HPal_v2.create: Warrior pressure → fresh Warrior control → Paladin stuns/damage; track each current Trinket.
SPR_vs_Arms_HPal_v2.convert: After Warrior escape use, renewed control supports a Paladin go. Renew Paladin control after its escape.
SPR_vs_Arms_HPal_v2.alternative: Continue Warrior through partial heals; renew stuns and interrupt Paladin healing.
SPR_vs_Arms_HPal_v2.failure: Protection or healing can erase the healer attempt before friendly survival allows another.
SPR_vs_Arms_HPal_v2.reset: On Shield, pressure Warrior or stabilize; rebuild control for a post-immunity Paladin return.

SPR_vs_Disc_Feral_v2.start: Feral, with Priest control; keep attacking through initial absorbs.
SPR_vs_Disc_Feral_v2.objective: Build repeated Feral attacks with renewed healer disruption.
SPR_vs_Disc_Feral_v2.win: Feral remains damaged into renewed stuns, or Priest takes damage while Feral is contained.
SPR_vs_Disc_Feral_v2.create: Renew Feral stuns with Priest Gouge/Silence/Fear; track each escape separately.
SPR_vs_Disc_Feral_v2.convert: Repeat Feral after partial heals. Fresh Feral control supports a documented Priest alternative.
SPR_vs_Disc_Feral_v2.alternative: Feral escape → Blind/Sap → Priest occurs; short Fear/stun swaps also occur with escapes retained.
SPR_vs_Disc_Feral_v2.failure: Two losses: stalled attacks and friendly collapse; one Priest attempt is interrupted by Cyclone.
SPR_vs_Disc_Feral_v2.reset: Recover and rebuild an attack after healing or Cyclone; resumed Feral pressure is documented.

SPR_vs_Balance_Sub_v1.create: Both opening targets recur; the choice trigger is unknown.
SPR_vs_Balance_Sub_v1.convert: Rogue dies more often, but direct Druid finishes also repeat.
SPR_vs_Balance_Sub_v1.alternative: A healed Druid attempt can lead to a Rogue switch.
SPR_vs_Balance_Sub_v1.failure: Druid healing restores the target before friendly survival fails.
SPR_vs_Balance_Sub_v1.reset: Renew pressure and Druid disruption after recovery.

SPR_vs_Arms_Disc_v1.start: Arms Warrior; recorded in 15/18 games. This is the labeled opening target, not necessarily the first sustained coordinated damage.

evidence.contradiction_scope: Only challenges to the explicitly rejected automatic-switch hypothesis, not a union of v1 universal-claim exceptions. Qualified defaults have separate alternative and failure evidence in claim_review.json.
data_quality_notes: Source extractions reviewed; original videos were not reopened during synthesis.
Both dedicated player-role fields are empty in all input records; roles remain unknown except where explicit narrative evidence is cited.
Sample win rate is a property of selected footage, not expected ladder performance.
Absent events are unknown unless the record explicitly establishes availability or absence.
A reported enemy kill can occur after a friendly death; the round result is stored separately.
18 records carry source quality flags; consult evidence and exceptions before treating a claim as footage-verified.

All scoped matches have individually authored decision episodes; unresolved timing, phase and pre-choice states remain explicit. Review status reviewed_with_gaps reflects extraction limits, not skipped records.

facts.sequence_limit: Endpoints only. No intermediate swap timing, causal sequence, or survival at the enemy death is inferred by this computation.

hypotheses.statement: Start on enemy Rogue with enemy Priest Sap/control. The recorded Rogue opener is the default, but some labels reflect chip damage or absorbed attacks; Priest-first commitments also recur.
hypotheses.limitation: The opener may primarily threaten Rogue, with a Priest opportunity emerging from spread damage, control or unrecorded accessibility. Escape use, healing and later control do not uniquely predict the chosen target; some control starts after the switch.

hypotheses.statement: The Rogue opener serves two observed continuations: a direct or repeated Rogue attack with Priest disruption, and a Priest commitment supported by renewed Rogue control. Escape depletion can create the second opportunity, but the evidence does not establish one compulsory conversion or a preference between them.

failure_modes.text: Healer commitments can reach low health, meet protection or healing, and fail to recreate that deficit before friendly survival ends. Control/resource progress does not measure remaining friendly capacity to finish. A Paladin kill can also be followed by a lost Warrior cleanup.

hypotheses.statement: Start on Feral with Priest control. Repeated Feral damage/stuns form the observed default; absorbed attacks remain real commitments, while selecting Priest for control does not establish a healer damage opener.
hypotheses.limitation: Feral may be a setup target for a Priest go in some games, but deep recovered Feral attacks are repeatedly renewed on Feral. Fast healer switches also follow nearly undamaged Feral openers; healing alone is not a discriminator.

failure_modes.text: The two losses are distinct: one has repeated healed Feral attempts, then Cyclone-stalled Priest pressure and Rogue death; the other has an absorbed Priest opener, shallow healed Feral damage and rapid friendly Priest death. Neither is a well-established common error or universal Cyclone failure rule.
